text: The glass gives her no answer. But Nib has found a crack beside it, where the cables snake through.
Jaeha offers the crew a way out of seeing this. Pyo has looked away long enough.
Single file, they follow the cables down an old stone corridor.
And at its end, Jaeha stops dead. A tall iron door, propped open, violet light beyond it.
The colour drains out of the world.
Four years ago, a young Jaeha hammered on this same door from the other side.
Just inside it lies a rusted hard-hat lamp, and under it, a strip of faded orange vest.
Jaeha picks the lamp up, very gently.
Nib swings the door wider. Scratched deep into its inside: everyone comes back. And a little thumbs-up.
Jaeha kneels and traces the letters. Shut in here, hyung still found the strength to carve his rule.
Nib rests a hand on his shoulder. Behind him, the crew take off their hard hats, one by one.
Moon Ahin puts it together: the man from the stream. Jaeha clips the lamp to his belt and stands.
They crawl out onto an old stone balcony, and violet light rises over the balustrade like a sunrise.
Below, a pit a hundred and fifty metres wide, full of machinery. In its centre kneels a chained sea-giant in coral armour, pipes driven into his body.
The window reads like a stock list: the Hushed Tide Warden, restrained, kept alive by machine, milked for four years. That's why the gate never closed.
A tear of seawater runs down the giant's face.
The pipes pulse violet in time with his heartbeat.
In rows of glass tanks, the light settles into cores, each cap stamped with the hexagon and the crescent-moon seal.
Engineers work around him like dairy farmers. One leans on a chain, eating a sandwich.
Pyo finally has his answer, and he crushes his hard hat in both hands.
Lyra goes white. She knows him from old songs: a legend of her world, kneeling in a hole.
Nib shakes, knuckles white on his knives. They didn't just beat a hero. They turned him into a tap.
Under Borro's hands, the stone balustrade cracks.
Moon Ahin raises her phone, and Jaeha's hand closes over it. One flash, and the whole pit looks up.
A guard's torch sweeps up the wall toward them.
Everyone lies flat. Ho clamps both hands over his nose. The beam slides past.
Moon Ahin stares at her grandfather's crescent on a tank cap. Her family's cores keep half of Seoul's hospitals running.
Now she has seen the source.
Jaeha copies out the rule every child knows, and under it a line pressed so hard it tears the paper. Kanghan found the loophole.
The official record called this gate finished. Jaeha's cold eyes see a farm, worked every day since hyung died.
Through Nib's eyes, from under a catwalk, Jaeha studies the chain: black factory steel, with one small stamped mark.
From his pocket, he takes a small black chain link.
The last link of the knight's chains, when the rest crumbled to dust.
Held up beside the giant chain, the marks match. Gate 0912, where it all began, was Kanghan's too.
Nib drops back onto the balcony and freezes at the sight of it.
He knows what that link means before anyone says it. Whoever chained this giant also chained his commander.
His knives slide out, and he turns toward the pit. Jaeha catches his wrist, holds on, and makes him a promise.
Trembling, Nib puts the knives away.
Moon Ahin says the cold, practical thing: shut this down, and hospital patients pay. Jaeha refuses the choice.
Pyo can't look again. Every trap his crew sprang cleared the road for the men who run this.
Ho stares at his hands, thinking of the chicken shop. Woo knows what that money was made of, and doesn't want to hear it.
A freight elevator carries racks of glowing tanks up past them, toward the city.
Jaeha watches it rise toward Seoul, jaw tight. Those tanks aren't carrying light. They're carrying the giant's life.
Then the Warden's chained hand twitches, and the chain snaps taut against the wall.
The sandwich engineer jumps back and drops his lunch into the pit.
In the control room, every gauge swings into the red. The engineer watching them calls the giant it.
The Warden's huge eyelid trembles.
Borro feels it first: the giant has noticed them. Lyra doesn't understand. They've stayed perfectly still.
Jaeha understands. His summons come from the giant's world, the first he has sensed in four years.
The scanners have noticed them too: three summons nobody registered, on that exact balcony.
An engineer jumps up and points straight at them.
Every light turns red, sirens wail, and guards run for the north wall. And the Warden's head lifts, just a fraction.
Moon Ahin states the obvious, white-faced. Jaeha is already up, sending them back the way they came with the oldest order he knows.
Black boots pound up a steel stair.
Below, a guard captain points his radio up at the balcony and seals their way out.
Through Nib's eyes: torch beams filling the far end of the passage they came in by.
Lights below, lights behind, and every face on the balcony turns to Jaeha.
Across the pit, the Warden's eyelid lifts by a hair. Beneath it, a sliver of deep sea-green.
Trapped from both sides, Jaeha calmly opens his notebook to a blank page, and asks for the one thing they're out of: time.
